In [[category theory]], a branch of mathematics, a '''subterminal object''' is an object ''X'' of a [[category (mathematics)|category]] ''C'' with the property that every object of ''C'' has at most one [[morphism]] into ''X''.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GJRQAAAAMAAJ|title=Category Theory and Computer Science: 6th International Conference, CTCS '95, Cambridge, United Kingdom, August 7 - 11, 1995. Proceedings|first=David|last=Pitt|first2=David E.|last2=Rydeheard|first3=Peter|last3=Johnstone|date=12 September 1995|publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]]|access-date=18 February 2017}}</ref> If ''X'' is subterminal, then the pair of identity morphisms (1<sub>''X''</sub>, 1<sub>''X''</sub>) makes ''X'' into the [[product (category theory)|product]] of ''X'' and ''X''. If ''C'' has a [[terminal object]] 1, then an object ''X'' is subterminal if and only if it is a [[subobject]] of 1, hence the name.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HCiqCAAAQBAJ|title=Foundations of Software Science and Computational Structures: 13th International Conference, FOSSACS 2010, Held as Part of the Joint European Conferences on Theory and Practice of Software, ETAPS 2010, Paphos, Cyprus, March 20-28, 2010, Proceedings|first=Luke|last=Ong|date=10 March 2010|publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]]|isbn=9783642120329|access-date=18 February 2017}}</ref> The category of categories with subterminal objects and [[functor]]s preserving them is not [[accessible category|accessible]].<ref>{{cite journal|first=Michael|last=Barr|first2=Charles|last2=Wells|date=September 1992|title=On the limitations of sketches|magazine=Canadian Mathematical Bulletin|volume=35|issue=3|pages=287–294|publisher=[[Canadian Mathematical Society]]|doi=10.4153/CMB-1992-040-7|doi-access=free}}</ref>
